mission: Goodfire is a public benefit corporation that builds interpretability research and tools: methods to see inside neural networks, debug them, and steer how they learn. Its stated goal is to fully understand and align AI so humanity can trust superintelligence. It applies the same tools to scientific models, for example in genomics and Alzheimer's research.

key_work.title: Intentionally designing the future of AI
key_work.plain_summary: Goodfire's agenda: move from training AI by trial and error to deliberately designing what models learn, using interpretability.

key_work.title: Revealing the neural geometry inside models
key_work.plain_summary: Maps the geometric structure in a network's activations and shows it can be edited to control behaviour.

key_work.title: Surfacing unexpected behaviors caused by a training run
key_work.plain_summary: Amplifies the difference between two checkpoints to expose rare bad behaviours that evaluations miss; Goodfire says it is now used in pre-deployment testing of frontier models.

key_work.title: Reducing hallucinations with features as rewards
key_work.plain_summary: Using interpretable internal features as the training reward cut hallucinations by 58% at much lower cost than using an LLM judge.

key_work.title: Detecting performative chain-of-thought
key_work.plain_summary: Probes show models often 'know' their answer but keep generating reasoning anyway; detecting this saved up to 68% of tokens.

key_work.title: Interpreting language model parameters
key_work.plain_summary: Interprets a model's weights directly rather than its activations (parameter decomposition).

key_work.title: Discovering a novel class of Alzheimer's biomarkers
key_work.plain_summary: Reverse-engineering a biology foundation model surfaced new candidate biomarkers for Alzheimer's detection.

funding_note: Site says it has raised over $200M from investors including Menlo, Lightspeed and B Capital.

warnings.text: We train today's most consequential technology with remarkably little understanding of how it works.
Training often causes rare, undesired behaviours that ordinary evaluations miss.
Models can produce 'performative' reasoning that does not reflect how they reach answers.

recommendations.text: Make interpretability central to building AI, so models are designed rather than grown by trial and error.
Use interpretability to debug training data and runs before deployment.
Use internal features to guide training (for example, to reduce hallucinations).
